chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Musa from Ahmad ibn Umar from Yahya ibn Aban from Shihab said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'If the people knew how Allah, Blessed and High, created this creation, no one would blame another.' So I said, 'May Allah keep you well! How is that?' He said?' He said: 'Indeed, Allah, Blessed and High, created parts reaching forty-nine parts. Then He made the parts into tenths, thus making the part ten tenths. Then He distributed it among the creation.'

So He placed in one man a tenth of a part, and in another two-tenths of a part, until reaching a complete part; and in another a part and a tenth of a part, and another a part and two-tenths of a part, and another a part and three-tenths of a part, until reaching two complete parts. Then by that calculation, until reaching with the highest of them forty-nine parts.

So the one in whom there is only a tenth of a part cannot be like the owner of the two-tenths; and similarly, the owner of the two-tenths cannot be like the owner of the three-tenths; and similarly, the one for whom a part is complete cannot be like the owner of the two parts. And if the people knew that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created this creation upon this, no one would blame another.
ai.seo_question: What is the theological explanation for differences in human capacity and why no one should blame another?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the concept of divine predestination (al-Jabr) by describing human creation as a distribution of forty-nine parts, where each individual receives a specific, fixed measure of capacity or intellect. This scholarly explanation emphasizes that differences in ability are not due to merit or effort alone but are inherent divine allocations, thereby fostering humility and eliminating mutual blame among people. The narration serves as a foundational text for understanding the balance between divine decree and human responsibility in Shia theology.
